full_details: In the morning the towers and their gilt vanes stood across the frosted Green. The waiting was in a passage and then in a plain room, and it was longer than anyone liked. You told Sam yesterday about ten. The house had nine, after supper. You did not mend either hour. At the inn you read the line you enter on, and no second line. At half past five the service room had a few tallow candles, a small fire, a rolled part, and a gilt crown set out of the way. Through the door the hall was a hundred white tapers over sweet-flag rushes, and the canopy of state had nobody under it. Sam bowed to it through the door. You went in first, in a paper crown and the old velvet, and you did not look at the state. She laughed once, aloud, from deep in the chest, at Pope's Armado. Kemp spoke what was set down and three lines over, to her face, and her hand lifted. At the last Sincler came on in black, and the hall stayed quiet through the owl until the chair stirred. Bryan said she kept her seat to the songs, as good as a purse and likelier. In the buttery my lord clapped your shoulder hard enough to rattle what teeth you have left, and went out without a word. Nothing was paid.
one_sentence: You waited on an empty chair, went in first on the old line, and came away with one laugh.
title: Went in first, and she laughed once
